belief: Because I am divorced, God can’t use me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that because you are divorced God can’t use you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Church policies that kept divorced people from serving. Shame or judgment from other Christians. Grief over a marriage that ended, whether or not it was your choice. Verses about divorce used without grace. Feeling like a failure or second-class Christian.
teaches: God takes marriage seriously, and divorce is painful. But divorce is not beyond God’s grace or His purposes. God says, “Behold, I am about to do something new.” Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman who had been married five times, and many in her town believed because of her testimony. God promises to repay the years the locusts have eaten, and to work all things together for good for those who love Him. Your story is not over.
self_statements: God can’t use someone who failed at marriage.
I have nothing to offer God.
Everyone at church sees me as a failure.
errors: Defining yourself by one painful event.
Turning “my marriage ended” into “my usefulness to God ended.”
Assuming everyone sees you as a failure.
Overlooking God’s pattern of using broken people.
questions: Whom did Jesus use to reach a whole town in John 4?
What does God say He is about to do in Isaiah 43:19?
Does God work only through people with perfect histories?
What has God taught me through this pain that could help others?
Have I brought any part of this I need to confess to God?
Is the judgment I fear coming from God or from people?
How might God want to use me now?
truth: My divorce does not disqualify me from being used by God. He is doing something new in my life. God used a woman with a broken history to bring a whole town to Jesus, and He can use me. He can restore what was lost and work even this together for good.
hw_questions: Whom did Jesus use to reach a town?
What is God about to do?
Does God use only perfect people?
What has this pain taught me that could help others?
Is the judgment I fear from God or people?
How might God use me now?
hw_truths: My divorce does not disqualify me.
God is doing something new in my life.
God uses people with broken stories.
God can restore the years that were lost.
God works all things together for good.
In Christ I am a new creation.
log: Each day, write one new thing God is doing in my life or one way He used me.
name_example: Behold, I am about to do something new in Sarah’s life; even now it is coming. Does she not see it? Indeed, I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
actions: and write how Jesus treated the woman and what happened afterward.
Serve in one small way this week,
and notice how God uses you.
including where you have seen God’s grace.
Talk with a pastor about serving,
and ask about divorce recovery support.
prayer: Father, thank You that my divorce is not the end of my story. Help me reject the lie that You can’t use me. Heal my heart, forgive what needs forgiving, and do something new in my life. Use my story to bring hope to others. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: God can work through imperfect people without waiting for them to become flawless.
God’s renewing work offers hope beyond failure, decay, and loss.
God’s story continues beyond a painful or confusing chapter.
Kristyn Getty with Vince Gill, Ellie Holcomb and Sierra Hull
